page.failureTail: Nothing moved — the registry is back as it was.

providers.note: Docker for dev and compose, Kubernetes for prod — the two IComputeProvider implementations v1 has. One takes new starts; the rest hold the leases they already handed out.
providers.emptyFiltered: no providers match the current filters
providers.handWork: Hand new starts to this provider

pools.note: Scaling is quota-aware plus the provider's capacity api, so every pool has two ceilings with two different owners. The one marked <tag>binding</tag> is the one refusing the next container — the other is what it had spare.

sentences.noAnswer: capacity api did not answer — no ceiling can be read for this pool
sentences.bothFull: quota and cluster are both full — nothing can start here
sentences.both: quota and cluster agree — room for {{slots}}
sentences.quotaFull: quota is the ceiling — nothing can start, and the cluster still has {{slots}} free
sentences.quota: quota is the ceiling — room for {{slots}}, with {{spare}} free on the cluster
sentences.clusterFull: the cluster is the ceiling — nothing can start, and the quota still allows {{slots}}
sentences.cluster: the cluster is the ceiling — room for {{slots}}, with {{spare}} left under the quota

versions.note: A worker is labelled by image digest and profiles git-ref. Changing either only affects a new start — an idle worker on any other label is never matched to an item, which is how a full pool sits beside a growing queue.
versions.emptyFiltered: no labels match the current filters
versions.strandedTitle: {{count}} idle on a label nothing is matched to — they will not claim an item
versions.retireTooltip: Retire the idle workers on this label
versions.retireTitle: Retire the idle workers on this label?
versions.retireBody: {{label}} — {{idle}} idle containers are torn down. The {{rest}} still holding a lease keep running until their item lands.

reason.both: image and profiles ref both moved
reason.image: a release behind on the image
reason.profiles: same image, the profiles ref moved

boards.note: The grafana boards, folded in from the screen that used to own them. They open in a new tab and are not embedded here on purpose: infra metrics and a run's own timeline are read on different clocks by people asking different questions, and a surface that showed both would teach an operator to look for a run's story in a metrics board, where only half of it is. A run's story is on /runs. One board covers every project at once, and the definitions are versioned with the platform — the guide under the list says how to connect an installation that has nothing in it yet.
